subject: Trump's 'voluntary exit offer', and the Statue of Liberty
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: on a white background, Donald Trump stands on the left — blond hair, a pink face, a dark blue suit, white shirt and red tie. With both hands he holds out a pink sheet on which, in large black capitals, is written: VOLUNTARY EXIT OFFER, with four ruled lines below. On the right stands the Statue of Liberty in blue-green, the crown on her head and her tablet held on the left; her right hand rests at the edge of the paper. At the bottom right lies a newspaper cutting that reads: AFTER MICROSOFT & GOOGLE, META LAUNCHES VOLUNTARY EXIT PLANS FOR ITS EMPLOYEES. Bottom left, the cartoonist's signature: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: Trump holds out a pink sheet to the Statue of Liberty: VOLUNTARY EXIT OFFER. It is the same offer the big tech companies are making to their employees — and the newspaper cutting on the floor says as much: after Microsoft and Google, Meta too has announced voluntary exit plans for its staff.

The joke is that the ‘voluntary exit’ form has now reached the statue of freedom itself. In the country that was known for giving the world's people a place, Trump stands like a boss handing Lady Liberty the paper. The language of shedding staff is now being applied to a country's image: first the companies let people go ‘voluntarily’, now it is the turn of the ideal that made America America.
